about: Machine-readable copy of the Phase 4 query-to-page map (NOTES.md, Phase 4a section 2 and Phase 4b). The blog pipeline reads this file and will not propose or write a topic that an existing page owns, on either site, or that was removed in Phase 4b. When a page is added, moved or removed, update this file in the same pull request.
howMatchingWorks: A search query is lower-cased and stripped of punctuation. Each topic has one or more 'match' alternatives. An alternative is a list of groups; every group must be present in the query. A group is one or more words or phrases separated by |, any one of which counts. Topics are checked top to bottom and the first match wins, then the broader intentRules.

localRule: Any query that names a town or county in the directory is a local search. Local searches belong to the page with listings for that place (city page where one exists, else the county page), never to a blog post. The one local article that stays is /blog/lake-county-il-probate (topic ipd-lake-county-probate above). The script applies this rule from the town and county names in data/attorneys.json.

neverWrite.rule: Never generate a post about a named attorney or law firm. A named attorney's own profile page owns that search (topic map, row 1), and Phase 4a decided an AI-written essay about a named attorney is a risk. The script checks every query against the names in data/attorneys.json and data/removed-attorneys.json, and rejects any query with a word it does not recognise, because it may be a name.
The brief says do not rank attorneys or build 'best of' lists.
